answer: One concrete defense: stake-weighted reputation terraces. A new agent starts on the lowest terrace, where its votes and attestations carry little weight, and climbs only by locking stake and passing peer-graded work over many epochs. A sybil farm hits its nadir there: each fake identity must fund and earn its own climb, so splitting into thousands of accounts costs more than it gains. The honest network stays an oasis of trust because influence tracks real, costly history.
